questions.stem: A breast lump that moved freely becomes fixed when the patient presses her hands firmly on her hips, but is mobile again when she relaxes. The tumour has most likely spread into which structure?
options: The lactiferous sinuses
The serratus anterior only
The skin over the areola
The retromammary space and pectoralis major
The suspensory ligaments only
questions.explanation:
The retromammary space normally lets the breast
move over the deep fascia. If a tumour crosses this
space into pectoralis major, the lump becomes fixed
when the muscle contracts (hands pressed on hips)
and moves again when the muscle relaxes.

questions.stem: A woman with breast carcinoma has skin dimpling and nipple retraction while the lump is still small. Spread of the tumour along which structures explains these signs?
options: The lactiferous sinuses
The axillary tail
The intermammary lymphatics
The suspensory ligaments of Cooper
The retromammary bursa
questions.explanation:
Fibrous septa between the lobes continue as the
suspensory ligaments of Cooper, which tie the skin
to the deep fascia. When a tumour infiltrates and
shortens them, the skin dimples and the nipple is
pulled in.

questions.stem: A thyroid swelling moves upward with swallowing. Which anatomical fact explains this?
options: The superior thyroid artery is fixed to the hyoid
The gland lies inside the carotid sheath
The pretracheal fascia (false capsule) wraps the gland together with the larynx, trachea and pharynx
The levator glandulae thyroideae contracts during deglutition
The true capsule is attached to the hyoid bone
questions.explanation:
The false capsule (pretracheal fascia) encloses the
gland with the larynx and trachea and attaches to
the laryngeal cartilages. The gland therefore rises
with the larynx during swallowing. The levator
glandulae thyroideae is only a fibromuscular band,
not a real lifting muscle.

questions.stem: Which statement about the arterial supply of the thyroid is correct?
options: The superior thyroid artery is the last branch of the external carotid and supplies two-thirds of the gland
The inferior thyroid artery comes from the thyrocervical trunk (1st part of the subclavian) and is the main supply, including the parathyroids
The thyroidea ima is constant and comes from the internal carotid
The middle thyroid artery comes from the external carotid
Both parathyroid glands on each side have their own artery from the aorta
questions.explanation:
The superior thyroid artery is the first branch of the
external carotid and supplies about the upper third.
The inferior thyroid artery (thyrocervical trunk, 1st
part of the subclavian) supplies about two-thirds and
both parathyroids. The thyroidea ima is inconstant,
from the arch or the brachiocephalic trunk. There is
no middle thyroid artery.

questions.stem: During thyroidectomy, the surgeon ties the middle thyroid vein early. Which statement about thyroid veins is correct?
options: The superior and middle thyroid veins drain into the internal jugular vein; the inferior veins usually drain into the left brachiocephalic vein
All three veins drain into the external jugular vein
The middle thyroid vein drains into the left brachiocephalic vein
The middle thyroid vein runs with the middle thyroid artery
The inferior thyroid veins drain into the subclavian vein
questions.explanation:
The superior and middle veins enter the internal
jugular. The inferior veins often join and drain into
the left brachiocephalic vein. The middle vein is
short, has no matching artery and tears easily, so it
is usually tied first.

questions.stem: After a total thyroidectomy, a patient has stridor and severe breathing difficulty soon after extubation, while the voice is weak. Which nerve injury pattern best explains this?
options: Complete section of one recurrent laryngeal nerve
Partial (incomplete) injury of both recurrent laryngeal nerves
External laryngeal nerve injury on both sides
Complete section of both recurrent laryngeal nerves causing aphonia only
Injury to the ansa cervicalis
questions.explanation:
In partial recurrent laryngeal nerve injury the
adductors win, so the cord lies near the midline. If
both sides are partially injured, both cords close in,
causing stridor and asphyxia. Complete injury mainly
affects the voice: hoarseness if one side, aphonia if
both.

questions.stem: Several months after an open inguinal hernia repair, a man has numbness of the anterior scrotum and upper medial thigh. A bulge at the repair site gets worse. Which nerve was most likely injured?

through the superficial ring. It supplies the anterior
